text:
maria: Heads up — seeing a mismatch between offload telemetry (bytes_offloaded) and allocator residency counters after yesterday's rolling deploy. Cost dashboard shows ~18% more offload egress than our allocator thinks.

tomas: any clear repro? load pattern? :thinking_face:

maria: Small repro on staging: run a bursty chat workload (short prompts) vs long-context batch. Metrics: offload_bytes spikes, allocator.evicted_bytes stays flat. snippet:
```
# dev run
./perf_runner --profile bursty_chat --duration 5m
# metrics
offload_bytes: 1.2GB
allocator.evicted_bytes: 200MB
```

alex: that smells like telemetry emission timing. We aggregate per-minute; allocator counters are cumulative flush-on-rotate — could be missing flush windows during deploy.

sasha: also check our prefix/KV cache path: if KV cache serves from host backing, it might not increment the allocator eviction counter (we only instrument GPU-resident evicts). We added a host-backed path last month.

maria: good call. I toggled host-backed and saw offload drop but billing still reported earlier spike. So two problems: (1) evicts not instrumented for host-path, (2) billing window uses offload_bytes raw stream (no de-dupe).

tomas: proposed quick fixes:
- instrument host-backed eviction hooks to call Allocator.RecordEvict(size)
- add a reconciliation job that joins offload events with allocator counters per-tenant hourly and emits diffs
- short-term: roll back a deploy change that changed emission ordering

alex: for reconciliation, prefer run in reconcile mode (best-effort) not to affect production pipeline. We should store (offload_event_id, tenant, size, timestamp) and join on time ranges + request id.

sasha: note: request ids can be missing on internal cache hits. We should fallback to tenant+time+route heuristics.

maria: okay. I'll open an RFC-ish PR for the instrumentation change + a small reconciliation job. For now, can we add a temporary alert when offload_bytes > allocator_evicted_bytes * 1.15 for 5m? want to catch spikes.

infra-bot: alert rule created: offload_vs_allocator_mismatch (severity: P2) — firing only for staging/production groups. See runbook: /runbooks/offload-mismatch

tomas: followups for the RFC: include API for 'EvictSource' so we can tag host-backed vs gpu-evict. Add unit test that simulates double-counting edge case.

alex: also track billing mapping: if reconciliation shows persistent mismatch for a tenant, pausing billing exports for that tenant until we verify would avoid overcharge incidents.

maria: listed next actions in the PR description. I'll link the perf logs and example trace ids. thanks all :thumbsup:

sasha: one more — add a propagating trace/span id on cache hits. Makes joins trivial.

maria: will add. last note: low-priority but add a telemetry schema version field so we can guard against deploy ordering mismatches.

tomas: agreed. good triage session.
